# How to Run Your First Viral ChatGPT Trend Prompt From Start to Finish

> **In short:** You can copy a trend prompt, paste it into ChatGPT, fill in your own details, and decide whether the answer is worth keeping. Nothing guarantees a post goes viral, so check every fact and never share private information.

Trend prompts are short instructions that many people copy and personalize, such as "write a funny caption about my week" or "describe my morning routine as a movie trailer." This guide walks you through one complete run, from finding the prompt to deciding whether to keep the result. It is written for complete beginners.

## Before you start

- **A ChatGPT account.** You can use the ChatGPT website or app. Some features may need a paid plan, so check your account settings if something is locked.
- **A trend prompt you trust.** Copy one from a source you already read, not from a random link.
- **A notes app, about 20 minutes, and an open mind.** Expect to run the prompt two or three times before you like the result.

## Step 1 — Find a trend prompt and copy it

Find a prompt you like in a post, article or caption, and select all of its text. Most devices let you press and hold the text, then tap a "Copy" option, or use the copy shortcut on a computer. Paste it into your notes app so you have a safe copy to edit.

Read the whole prompt before you move on. Look for square brackets, blanks or words like "your job" or "your city." Those are the spots you will personalize in Step 3. If the prompt asks you to upload a photo of another person, stop and skip it unless that person has agreed.

If you cannot copy the text, try typing it out by hand, or ask a friend to send you the words in a message you can copy from.

You'll know it worked when the full prompt sits in your notes app, and you can point to the spots that need your details.

## Step 2 — Open a new chat and paste the prompt

Open ChatGPT and start a new chat, which usually means tapping a button that looks like a pencil on a page or a plus sign. You should see an empty chat with a message box at the bottom of the screen. Tap inside that box, then paste your copied prompt.

When you paste, the full text appears in the message box. Nothing has been sent yet, so you can still edit it. Leave the text as it is for now. Your personal details come next.

If you do not see a message box, look for a text field near the bottom of the screen or a button that says something like "New chat" or uses a pencil icon. Layouts differ between phones and computers, so take a moment to scan the screen.

💬 Example: "Write a short, funny caption for a photo of [your pet] doing [everyday activity]."

You'll know it worked when your pasted text is visible in the message box, ready to edit.

## Step 3 — Swap in your own details

Now replace each bracketed or blank spot with your own information. Keep the sentence structure, but change the words that describe you. Use only details you are comfortable sharing, such as a hobby, a job title or a general city. Leave out your home address, phone number, passwords, and anything about other people that they have not agreed to share.

Tap inside the message box and edit the text. If the prompt says "[your job]," type your real job or a general version of it, such as "nurse," "teacher" or "warehouse worker." Keep your edits short so the prompt still reads clearly.

If the message box is hard to edit, select the text you want to change and type over it. If you accidentally delete the whole prompt, paste the copy from your notes app again.

💬 Example: "Rewrite this for my life: I'm a [job title] in [your city] who loves [hobby]."

You'll know it worked when the prompt reads like a sentence about you and contains no leftover brackets.

## Step 4 — Send it and read the first answer

Tap the send button, which is usually an arrow or paper-plane icon at the right edge of the message box. Your message will appear in the chat, and ChatGPT's answer will show up below it, often appearing word by word. Wait until the answer stops moving before you judge it.

Read it once for the big picture. If it misses the point, do not start over. Send a follow-up message that asks for a specific change. ChatGPT can adjust a draft quickly, but it cannot know your real life unless you tell it.

If nothing happens after you send, check your internet connection and try again. If you see a message about limits, you may need to wait or check your plan.

💬 Example: "Make this shorter, keep the humor, and remove any joke about [topic you dislike]."

You'll know it worked when a new answer appears under your last message, and it reflects your change.

## Step 5 — Judge whether the result is worth keeping

This step is the most important one. Read the answer slowly and ask yourself four questions. Does it sound like you, or like a stranger? Does it make any claim about a real person, company or fact? Would you feel comfortable if a stranger read it? Is it actually funny, useful or interesting to you?

If a fact or a claim looks wrong, check it with a trusted source before you use it. ChatGPT can write confident sentences that are simply incorrect, so treat its output as a draft, not a final answer. Ask it to list any claims you should verify.

If the result fails any check, that is useful information. It tells you what to change in your next message.

💬 Example: "List every factual claim in your last answer so I can check each one before I post it."

You'll know it worked when you have a short list of claims to verify, or you feel confident the draft passes all four questions.

## Step 6 — Save your favorite version

When you have a result you like, copy it into your notes app and label it with the date and the prompt name. That way you can find it later. Your chat history may also keep the conversation, usually in a sidebar or menu, so you can return to it.

Before you post anything, reread the final version once more. Remove any detail you do not want public. If you plan to share a photo, make sure it shows nothing private, such as a street sign or a document.

If you cannot find your old chat, rely on your notes copy. That copy is your safest backup.

💬 Example: "Give me the final version in plain text with no headings so I can paste it into my notes."

You'll know it worked when your finished draft is saved outside the chat, and you have reread it once before sharing.

## Common mistakes

- **Posting without checking.** A trend prompt can produce a claim that sounds right but is wrong. The fix is to run Step 5 every time, and to verify any fact before it goes public.
- **Sharing private details.** Your full name, address or a photo of someone else can end up online. The fix is to use general details and ask people before you include them.
- **Expecting a guaranteed hit.** ChatGPT can write a good draft, but it cannot predict what will catch attention or go viral. The fix is to treat the result as one draft among many and enjoy the process.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You can use trend prompts to make a birthday card message, a funny family group caption or a quick travel plan, then adjust the result until it feels like you.
- **For your business or work:** A trend prompt can give you a starting point for a short social post or a slogan idea. Always check any claim, and keep your brand voice in the final version.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a low-stakes prompt for a private message to a friend, and practice Steps 4 and 5 before you try anything public.

## Try it now

Copy one trend prompt into your notes app, then send it to ChatGPT with one of your own details filled in. Read the answer and ask yourself the four questions from Step 5. You'll have a finished first run in about two minutes.
